items.title: The domination order on tableaux, Garnir tableaux and bricks
items.statement:
Retain English Young diagrams and row-reading initial standard tableau t^mu. For a mu-tableau T let w_T t^mu=T. The STRONG Bruhat order on tableaux is S<=_B T iff w_S<=w_T in the permutation Bruhat order. For tableaux write S\unlhd T for S<=_B T and S\lhd T for strict order; partition dominance has its separately declared meaning. For row-strict S,T this is equivalent to the prefix shape of S DOMINATING the prefix shape of T for every prefix; it is distinct from weak Bruhat order and must not reverse this dominance direction. The transposition criterion is S=(a1 b1)...(am bm)T with an<bn and bn occupying an earlier row-reading node than an at each backward step.

For entries r,s in one component define r right-arrow_T s when they lie in the SAME row and s is strictly to the right; r down-arrow_T s when they lie in the SAME column and s is strictly below; and r northeast_T s when s is strictly ABOVE and strictly RIGHT of r. Southwest is the reverse northeast relation. A weak Bruhat graph edge T --r--> S requires both tableaux standard, S=s_r T, and r occupying an earlier row-reading node than r+1. Equivalently r+1 northeast_T r, or r is in an earlier component than r+1. In particular a same-column or same-row swap is NOT a standard edge. Terminal paths are directed paths ending at T.

The Garnir belt at (a,b,n) consists of the row-a tail from b and the row-(a+1) prefix through b. Its Garnir tableau is the maximal standard tableau in the strong Bruhat order agreeing with t^mu outside that belt. A horizontal brick is a string of consecutive entries along SAME-row right arrows. The following source facts are retained with these exact conventions: the transposition/prefix-shape criterion; the row-strictness of a vertical swap and its exceptional-prefix comparison; agreement outside the Garnir belt for lower tableaux; and the four terminal alternatives for a horizontal or vertical consecutive pair. For a horizontal pair the last alternative is T=t^mu; for a vertical pair it is the corresponding Garnir tableau. These finite combinatorial facts are proved in the strategy. No choice.
items.strategy: Permutation Bruhat order is characterized by successive inversions of transpositions with the larger entry in an earlier position; placing these entries in row-reading positions gives the transposition criterion. For row-strict tableaux count the entries <=a in each row: the Bruhat rank inequalities are exactly dominance of their prefix row-count shapes, with S dominating T when w_S<=w_T. This proves the prefix criterion and its direction (the row-reading initial tableau is Bruhat-minimal and has dominant prefixes). A consecutive swap is standard exactly for strict northeast/southwest positions or different components; same-row and same-column pairs violate row/column increase. Combine this with earlier row-reading position to obtain the directed edge criterion. For a vertical consecutive swap, only prefix a=r changes; row-strictness is immediate and the exceptional-prefix comparison follows by moving its box between those two rows. Sorting each row converts the same transposition criterion to the row-strict Bruhat comparison. A tableau below a Garnir tableau can change only positions within its belt: outside row prefixes coincide, so the same rank inequalities force those entries to remain fixed. For a consecutive horizontal pair test, in order, existence of a distant terminal interchange preserving the pair, then the two adjacent terminal paths (r,r+1) and (r,r-1). If none exists, the positions r-1,...,1 and r+2,...,d are forced into row-reading order, hence T=t^mu. The identical test for a vertical pair forces exactly the maximal belt filling if none of the first three alternatives holds. This supplies the local terminal reductions used by the two-part graded-Specht induction; bricks are horizontal, not vertical chains. Actual BKW §§3.2–3.4 source proof and positional conditions checked, no finite sample computation substitutes for the general criterion. No choice.

items.statement: Let $A_{\mathbb Z}$ be a finite free unital integer algebra with $A_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q\otimes A_{\mathbb Z}$, and let $K$ be any characteristic-zero field. Suppose a finite-dimensional graded cyclic $A_K$-module $S_K$, with specified homogeneous generator $z_K$, is obtained from a homogeneous integer cyclic presentation $S_{\mathbb Z}=A_{\mathbb Z}/I_{\mathbb Z}$ by scalar extension, carrying $1+I_{\mathbb Z}$ to $z_K$. Suppose $S_K$ has a nonzero simple head $D_K$, with its specified grading normalization. Then the pair consisting of $D_K$ and the line spanned by the image $v$ of $z_K$ descends to $\mathbb Q$. More precisely there is a graded quotient $D_{\mathbb Q}$ of $S_{\mathbb Q}$ and $v_{\mathbb Q}\ne0$ such that $K\otimes D_{\mathbb Q}\cong D_K$ carries $1\otimes v_{\mathbb Q}$ to $v$. Consequently $A_{\mathbb Z}v$ is free of rank $\dim_KD_K$. If $D_K$ is absolutely simple, every nonzero quotient map from the specified $S_K$ to the fixed normalized $D_K$ has generator image on this same line, up to $K^\times$.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] [[thm-jacobson-radical-is-nilpotent-and-the-quotient-is-semisimple]] gives a nilpotent radical and semisimple quotient for every finite-dimensional algebra.

[F2] [[thm-wedderburn-artin-theorem]] and [[thm-simple-modules-over-semisimple-rings]] describe semisimple finite-dimensional algebras and their simples.

[F3] [[thm-schurs-lemma-for-modules]] applies to simple modules.

[F4] [[thm-irreducible-quotient-adjoins-a-root]] constructs a finite root field for a monic irreducible polynomial. A nonconstant characteristic polynomial has a monic irreducible factor by finite induction on degree.

[A1] The integer presentation is an explicit prerequisite, not asserted here for the existing Hecke Specht construction. Its identification must preserve the specified generator.

## Proof

**Given:** The hypotheses in the statement and F1–F4. All constructions involve finite-dimensional spaces and finite root fields; no Axiom of Choice is used.

1.1 We prove the regular-trace radical criterion directly over ANY characteristic-zero field $F$, without a splitting field or algebraic closure. Let $B$ be a finite-dimensional $F$-algebra and $\beta_B(a,b)=\operatorname{Tr}_F(L_{ab}:B\to B)$. Every element of $J(B)$ is orthogonal to $B$, because its product with any element lies in the nilpotent radical and hence has nilpotent left multiplication and zero trace. Choose a finite composition series of the left regular module. F1–F2 give $B/J(B)\cong\prod_iM_{n_i}(D_i)$, where each $D_i$ is a finite-dimensional division algebra over $F$; every simple composition factor is its column module $D_i^{n_i}$. Additivity of trace along the composition series shows that on this quotient the pairing is $\sum_i m_i\operatorname{Tr}_F(\rho_i(X_iY_i):D_i^{n_i}\to D_i^{n_i})$, where $m_i$ is the positive integer multiplicity of the column module in the regular composition series. Every $m_i$ is positive because the regular quotient already contains the corresponding column module. For a nonzero entry $x_{ab}$ of a block $X_i$, choose $Y_i$ with its only nonzero entry $(b,a)$ equal to $x_{ab}^{-1}$, and set all other blocks of $Y$ to zero. The product $X_iY_i$ has exactly one nonzero diagonal entry, namely $1$ at position $a$. On the $F$-space $D_i^{n_i}$, its action therefore has trace $\dim_F D_i$; off-diagonal blocks contribute no trace. The full pairing on this $Y$ is $m_i\dim_FD_i\ne0$ in characteristic zero. Thus the quotient pairing is nondegenerate and $\ker\beta_B=J(B)$. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 Apply step 1.1 over $F=\mathbb Q$ and $F=K$. The regular multiplication and trace matrices for $A_K$ are scalar extensions of those for $A_{\mathbb Q}$. Row reduction of a finite matrix commutes with field extension, so the kernels satisfy $\ker\beta_{A_K}=K\otimes\ker\beta_{A_{\mathbb Q}}$. The radical criterion gives $J(A_K)=K\otimes J(A_{\mathbb Q})$. This argument applies equally to nonsplit division factors and needs no separable splitting theorem. [step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 Put $S_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q\otimes S_{\mathbb Z}$ and $D_{\mathbb Q}=S_{\mathbb Q}/J(A_{\mathbb Q})S_{\mathbb Q}$. Tensoring quotient presentations is right exact and $K/\mathbb Q$ is flat, so $K\otimes D_{\mathbb Q}=S_K/J(A_K)S_K$. This last quotient is precisely the semisimple head: $A_K/J(A_K)$ is semisimple, so the quotient is semisimple, while every simple quotient kills $J(A_K)S_K$. Equivalently, intersections of maximal submodules equal $J(A_K)S_K$, since the intersection of the maximal submodules of a finite semisimple module is zero. The assumed head is simple, so this quotient is $D_K$. Its rational precursor is nonzero and simple: a proper nonzero rational submodule would remain proper and nonzero after faithful scalar extension. [F1, F2, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 The radical of a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q$-graded algebra is homogeneous. Indeed all scaling automorphisms $a_d\mapsto t^d a_d$ preserve its characteristic ideal $J$, for $t\in\mathbb Q^\times$. If $a=\sum_{d\in E}a_d\in J$ with finite degree set $E$, take $t=2^j$ for $j=0,\ldots,|E|-1$. The resulting coefficient matrix $((2^d)^j)_{j,d}$ is Vandermonde in the pairwise distinct rational numbers $2^d$, hence invertible; each $a_d$ is a rational linear combination of elements of $J$. Thus $J(A_{\mathbb Q})S_{\mathbb Q}$ is homogeneous and $D_{\mathbb Q}$ has the required quotient grading. Put $v_{\mathbb Q}=z_{\mathbb Q}+J(A_{\mathbb Q})S_{\mathbb Q}$. It is nonzero: otherwise cyclicity would force $D_{\mathbb Q}=0$. The scalar-extension quotient isomorphism preserves the generator, and hence its image is exactly $v$, including its degree. Any prescribed normalization shift is imposed simultaneously on both modules. [step 2.1, algebra]

3.1 The orbit $A_{\mathbb Z}v_{\mathbb Q}$ is generated as an abelian group by the images of a finite integer basis of $A_{\mathbb Z}$. It is torsion-free because it is a subgroup of a rational vector space. Its rational span is $D_{\mathbb Q}$, by cyclicity, so its rank equals $\dim_{\mathbb Q}D_{\mathbb Q}=\dim_KD_K$. The generator-preserving scalar-extension isomorphism identifies this orbit with $A_{\mathbb Z}v$. A finitely generated torsion-free abelian group is free, which proves the lattice assertion. [step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]

3.2 If a fixed normalized $D_K$ is absolutely simple, a nonzero map $S_K\to D_K$ is surjective and kills the radical. Since the head is already the simple $D_K$, such maps factor through its canonical quotient and differ by an invertible endomorphism of $D_K$. This endomorphism $f$ is scalar using a finite root-field construction. Its nonconstant characteristic polynomial has a monic irreducible factor; by F4 the corresponding quotient field $L/K$ supplies a root $\alpha$. The matrix $f_L-\alpha I$ has zero determinant and hence a nonzero kernel. Absolute simplicity makes $D_L$ simple, so this commuting endomorphism must be zero. Thus $f_L=\alpha I$, and any diagonal entry of the original $K$-matrix shows $\alpha\in K$. Thus every allowed generator image is a scalar multiple of the constructed image, and scaling the lattice preserves freeness and rank. No claim concerning an arbitrary vector in $D_K$ was used. [F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Extremal word characters detect normalized cyclotomic simple labels
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional standard homogeneous cyclotomic KLR module M over any field, choose a word by successive maximal last-color blocks i_1^{r_1}...i_s^{r_s}. There is exactly one normalized simple shift orbit S_c contributing to that word; its right crystal label is c=tilde f_{i_s}^{r_s}...tilde f_{i_1}^{r_1}u_Lambda. Its word graded dimension is product_a [r_a]_{i_a}!, and [M:S_c]_v equals gdim e(word)M divided by that product. All other simple orbits have zero word space. Consequently graded word characters are injective on G0. If two fields have modules with the same word character, their extremal words and detected canonical B(Lambda) labels coincide. No one-dimensional word-space assertion is made. Choice is inherited only through the existing abstract crystal identification.
items.strategy:
Let M be a finite-dimensional standard homogeneous cyclotomic module. Choose a nonzero word by successively maximizing the last constant-color block, then the preceding block after restricting that maximum, until the vacuum is reached. Write the resulting word as i_1^{r_1}...i_s^{r_s}, adjacent colors distinct. Restriction to a word idempotent is exact. Every simple constituent with nonzero word space must have precisely the same first maximal last-block length: a shorter length gives zero, a longer length would contradict maximality for M. The actual maximal-tail supplier identifies the full maximal restriction of this simple with N tensor L(i_s^{r_s}), where N is simple with zero residual i_s-tail. Repeat on N and on the corresponding exact restriction of M. At the end N is the unique vacuum simple. Reconstruct using the actual unique-head induction supplier. Hence exactly ONE simple shift orbit can contribute at the chosen word. Its crystal label is obtained by the same successive right-induction powers from the vacuum, so is field independent under the native11 canonical B(Lambda) identification.

For the normalized simple S in that orbit, maximal restriction is normalized N tensor normalized L(i^r): restriction commutes with finite vector duality, the two factors are absolutely simple, and their unique self-dual normalizations force the remaining shift to be zero. The normalized rank-r nil-Hecke simple has graded dimension [r]_i!, by the actual polynomial/corner calculation with shift -d_i binomial(r,2). Iterating gives gdim e(word)S=product_a [r_a]_{i_a}!. Therefore the coefficient of [S] in [M] is gdim e(word)M divided by this nonzero product. No one-dimensional Hom or semisimplicity shortcut is used. The same exact argument, ordering maximal tuples, shows that characters of normalized simples are linearly independent: choose the lexicographically maximal tuple with nonzero coefficient and evaluate its extremal word, then remove it. Thus graded word character equality implies G0 equality, over each original field.

 For character injectivity, realize the finite set of simple orbits appearing in a virtual relation as their direct sum, choose an extremal word as above, and evaluate the relation: exactly one orbit contributes, with its nonzero factorial polynomial. Its Laurent coefficient is zero. Remove it and repeat on the remaining finite set. This proves injectivity without assuming the relation is a module.

items.title: Standard Fock vectors expand in the upper global basis
items.statement:
Use the actual symmetric model M_mu=|mu transpose>, the basic field subspace V spanned by the restricted lower vectors G(lambda)=sum_mu d_(lambda,mu)(q) M_mu, and the bilinear form B(M_mu,M_nu)=delta_(mu,nu). Define the STANDARD COORDINATE FUNCTIONAL Std_mu in the RESTRICTED integral weight dual of the lower lattice by Std_mu(x)=B(x,M_mu). The restriction of B to V is nondegenerate; identify its field dual with V and denote by pi(M_mu) the vector representing Std_mu, equivalently the B-orthogonal projection of M_mu onto V. This is the definition of pi used below, not an undeclared projection from a generic upper-basis definition. If G^*(lambda) is the B/form-dual upper vector, then
$$Std_mu=pi(M_mu)=sum_{lambda restricted} d_(lambda,mu)(q) G^*(lambda).$$
At each content the restricted Std_lambda form an A-basis of the UPPER dual lattice, by the restricted dominance-unitriangular coefficient minor. The full family of raw M_mu is the basis of the ambient standard lattice; the full projected family Std_mu is generally redundant. Pi need not land in the LOWER integral lattice. In e2, G_11=M_11+q M_2 and G_11^*=(M_11+q M_2)/(1+q²), exhibiting the possible field denominator. The sums at fixed content are finite. Choice is inherited only from the declared global-basis suppliers.
items.strategy: At a fixed content let D have row mu and column lambda equal to d_(lambda,mu); its columns are the lower vectors in the standard basis. The restricted square minor is dominance-unitriangular, hence the columns are independent over Q(q). The Gram matrix is H=D^t D. A nonzero real specialization of q away from the finitely many denominators preserves the unitriangular minor, so those real columns have positive definite Gram matrix. Therefore det H is not the zero rational function. This proves nondegeneracy and defines the field orthogonal projection. For x=sum_lambda a_lambda G(lambda), Std_mu(x)=sum_lambda a_lambda d_(lambda,mu), proving integral values on the lower A-lattice. Evaluate on each G(lambda): the field/form-dual basis yields the displayed coefficient expansion. The restricted coefficient minor has determinant1 over A, so the corresponding Std_lambda form a basis of the upper dual; no inverse of1+q² is asserted to be a Laurent unit. Raw standard M_mu remain a basis of the ambient lattice, whereas projected standards can repeat the same upper weight space. The node polarization B(F_i x,y)=B(x,q^-1 K_i E_i y) and its inverse-adjoint formula show that V and V-perpendicular are invariant; pi therefore commutes with the field quantum action. In the symmetric linear-J convention E counts minus ABOVE, so E_i Std_mu=sum_remA q^(-d^A(mu)) Std_(mu minus A). This is exactly the canonical recursion used by the later Specht comparison, with no switch to the KK action. The actual original quantum reviewer supplied these guarded interfaces; no quantum9/23 source is altered. Choice only as inherited.

items.title: Graded module and projective Grothendieck groups of the KLR and Hecke towers
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $R=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q_+}R_\alpha$ be a tower of finite-dimensional unital $\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebras with local units $e(\alpha)$ summing to the identity of $R$ in the locally finite sense, each $R_\alpha$ a direct summand and $R_0=k$. Define $$K_0^{\rm gr}(R):=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q_+}K_0^{\rm gr}(R_\alpha),\qquad G_0^{\rm gr}(R):=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in Q_+}G_0^{\rm gr}(R_\alpha),$$ the restricted direct sums of the blockwise Grothendieck groups of [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]]: $K_0^{\rm gr}(R_\alpha)$ of finitely generated graded left $R_\alpha$-projectives modulo split exact sequences and $G_0^{\rm gr}(R_\alpha)$ of finite-dimensional graded left $R_\alpha$-modules modulo short exact sequences. Both are modules over $A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ by $q[M]:=[M\{1\}]$, and inside each finite-dimensional block the shift-orbit bases of [[thm-graded-projective-and-simple-classes-have-shift-orbit-bases]] hold. The Cartan homomorphism $c:K_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to G_0^{\rm gr}(R)$, $[P]\mapsto[P]$, is $A$-linear. The forgetful maps $\zeta$ to the ungraded groups $K_0(R)$, $G_0(R)$ are additive and satisfy $\zeta(qm)=m$. The groups $K_0^{\rm gr}$ and $G_0^{\rm gr}$ are DIFFERENT objects and are never identified.

**The two towers used below.** (i) For the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] at the level-one weight $\Lambda_0$ of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]], put $R^\Lambda_\alpha=R^\Lambda(\alpha)$; every block is finite dimensional and has the homogeneous symmetrizing functional of [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-algebras-are-finite-dimensional-graded-symmetric]], with grading shifts as in [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]. (ii) For the cyclotomic Hecke tower $H^{\Lambda}:=\bigoplus_\alpha H^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]] with the block decomposition of [[def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks]], fix an admissible local normalising series and transport the homogeneous KLR decomposition through the blockwise isomorphism of [[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]], as in [[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]; the induced transport identifies $K_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\cong K_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)$ as $A$-modules and similarly for $G_0^{\rm gr}$, compatibly with $\zeta$ and with the Cartan homomorphisms. Every class has finite root support, so the direct sums are restricted.

No choice principle is used in this definition.

items.title: The nondegenerate root-of-unity level-one Hecke regime
items.statement:
**Parameters.** Let $F$ be a field and $\xi\in F^\times$ with finite quantum characteristic $e=e(F,\xi)\in\{2,3,\dots\}$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]). We work in the NONDEGENERATE branch $\xi\ne1$; then $\xi$ is a primitive $e$-th root of unity in $F$, and all statements on this page live in one of the two sub-branches: (C0) $\operatorname{char}F=0$, or (CP) $\operatorname{char}F=p>0$ with $p\nmid e$. The Hecke parameter is written $\xi$ here; it is the letter $q$ of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]].

**Hecke side.** Fix the level-one fundamental weight $\Lambda_0$ of the cyclic affine type-$A$ datum with all $d_i=1$ and charge $0$ ([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). With the conventions of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]], $H^\Lambda_d=H_{F,\xi}(S_d)$ is the finite type-$A$ Hecke algebra $T_r^2=(\xi-1)T_r+\xi$ ([[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]]), and $H^\Lambda_\alpha=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d$ are its residue-content blocks ([[def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks]]).

**KLR side.** Use the type-$A$ specialization $Q^A$ of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]] with the same $e$ and the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]: the cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$, induction appends on the right, and the grading is $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$, $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ ([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). The transported grading on $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ uses a FIXED admissible local normalising series ([[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]); a different series gives a graded-isomorphic transported algebra via $\rho'\rho^{-1}$, and the graded multiplicities studied below do not depend on the choice.

**Grading and Fock variables.** All grading shifts and all global-basis polynomials are in the variable $q$, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. Thus $\xi\in F^\times$ (the Hecke parameter, equal to the source's $\xi$) and $q$ (the grading variable, equal to the source's quantum variable) are INDEPENDENT data; the design's phrase "Ariki's normalization $\xi=q^2$" is retained only as the source dictionary of [Ariki 1996], whose Hecke parameters are powers of a square $q_{\rm src}^2$, and no numerical relation or specialization between $\xi$ and $q$ is imposed.

**Fock side.** Use the level-one symmetric model $\mathcal F_{\rm sym}$ of [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]: charge $0$, node residues $c-r$, standard vectors $M_\mu$ for ALL partitions $\mu$, basic/restricted labels the $e$-restricted partitions $RP_\alpha=\{\lambda:\lambda_a-\lambda_{a+1}<e,\ \operatorname{cont}(\lambda)=\alpha\}$, empty component $B(\Lambda_0)$. For $\lambda\in RP$ the conjugate $\lambda'$ is $e$-regular. Write $P(\nu)$ for the independently constructed ordinary Dipper–James Specht module and $D_{\rm DJ}^{\nu}$ for its form quotient in [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]. Define $\theta(T_r)=(\xi-1)-T_r=-\xi T_r^{-1}$, the involutive sign automorphism of [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]. After converting right modules to left modules through the star anti-involution, the intrinsic restricted Murphy simple with label $\lambda$ is $\theta$-pullback of $D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'}$, not the untwisted ordinary module. This is an ungraded convention dictionary. The pullback can move blocks: on the multiplicative Jucys–Murphy elements $\theta(X_j)=X_j^{-1}$, so charge-zero residue content is sent from $\alpha$ to $-\alpha$. Thus the ordinary module before pullback has the conjugate content; no claim identifies it untwisted inside the same block. At $\xi=1$ the separate specialization theorem [[cor-dj-bridge-specialization-and-composition-multiplicity-dictionary]] identifies $\theta$ with sign tensoring over every field; $\xi=1$ remains outside the present nondegenerate regime.

No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: Direct convention check. At level one $(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)=\delta_{i,0}$, so the cyclotomic polynomial of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]] is $\prod_i(X_1-\xi^i)^{(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)}=X_1-1$ and the KLR cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$; the finite-characteristic hypothesis $e\in\{2,3,\dots\}$ makes $\xi\ne1$ a primitive $e$-th root, and in sub-branch (CP) the hypothesis $p\nmid e$ is exactly what makes a primitive $e$-th root exist in $F$. The type-$A$ datum and the grading are batch-24 clauses; the transport statement is the graded block isomorphism of [[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]] with [[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]. The Fock-side residues, the restricted labels and the empty component are batch-9/batch-23 clauses. The ordinary dictionary uses the actual universal module-and-form comparison [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]], not a rename of a cellular module. Its Laurent-unit form factor preserves radicals, including zero quotients, and gives $D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'}\cong(D_{\rm M}^{\lambda})^{\theta}$; apply the involution again. Right-to-left conversion sends $h\cdot m=m h^*$, and commutation $\theta *=*\theta$ preserves the same pullback dictionary. On the finite level-one tower $X_j=\xi^{1-j}T_{j-1}\cdots T_1^2\cdots T_{j-1}$. Applying $\theta(T_r)=-\xi T_r^{-1}$ to this palindrome gives $\theta(X_j)=X_j^{-1}$: the $2j-2$ signs cancel and the scalar is $\xi^{j-1}$. Generalized eigenvalues $\xi^i$ therefore become $\xi^{-i}$, proving the content reflection. No raw Hecke automorphism is claimed to preserve a fixed transported grading. The $\xi=1$ specialization is the separate arbitrary-field polytabloid specialization corollary, not an inference from a prime-field-only statement. The parameter dictionary is the naming clause of [BK 2009 §1 and §4.2] and [Ariki 1996 §1]; it makes no substitution. No choice is used.

items.title: The graded Cartan pairing between projective and module classes
items.statement:
In the situation and notation of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]], for each root degree $\alpha$, finite-dimensional graded left $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-modules $M$ and finitely generated graded projective $P$ put $$h_\alpha(P,M):=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_{R^\Lambda_\alpha}(P,M)=\sum_{d\in\mathbb Z}q^d\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}_{R^\Lambda_\alpha,d}(P,M)\in A .$$ By [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]] (whose finite-dimensional hypotheses hold blockwise) this descends to an $A$-sesquilinear pairing $$h:K_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)\times G_0^{\rm gr}(R^\Lambda)\longrightarrow A,$$ with the twist $q\mapsto q^{-1}$: $h(q^r[P],q^s[M])=q^{s-r}h([P],[M])$. In particular $h^0(P,S):=\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,S)$ is the degree-zero part. The pairing on the Hecke side is the transported pairing of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]]. Also fix the two dualities used below: the descended anti-involution $\psi$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]] with its finite-module duality $D_\psi$ and finite-projective duality $\#$, both shift-reversing and involutive on their domains; and the convention that a simple module or projective cover is called *normalized* when it is fixed (not merely fixed up to shift) by the relevant duality and, for a cover, when $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,S)=k$.

No perfectness, nondegeneracy or $A$-self-duality is asserted in this definition; those are supplied by [[thm-cyclotomic-klr-module-g-zero-is-the-dual-integral-highest-weight-module]] and its transported form on the Hecke side.
items.strategy: Specialize [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]] and [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]] to each finite-dimensional block $R^\Lambda_\alpha$; the finite support of the graded Hom spaces and the bilinearity/sesquilinearity reindexing are those of the cited theorem. Blockwise summability is the restricted sum of the previous definition. items.title: The graded Specht module by homogeneous standard tableaux
items.statement:
Work in the regime of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]]. Fix a partition $\mu$, put $d=|\mu|$, $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$, and let $K(\mu)$ be the $F$-span of the Murphy elements $m_{S,T}$ of [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] with $S,T$ standard tableaux of a multipartition strictly dominating $\mu$; by [[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]] $K(\mu)$ is a two-sided ideal of $H^\Lambda_d$ and $z_\mu:=m_{t^\mu t^\mu}+K(\mu)$ is defined. Define the (level-one) **cell/Specht module** $$S(\mu):=H^\Lambda_d\,z_\mu\subseteq H^\Lambda_d/K(\mu),$$ a LEFT $H^\Lambda_d$-module lying in the block $H^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For every standard $\mu$-tableau $T$ fix a reduced decomposition $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ of the associated permutation and put $z_T:=T_{w_T}z_\mu$, $v_T:=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ in the Khovanov-Lauda presentation of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]]. For a removable $i$-node $A$ of a partition $\lambda$ define $d_A(\lambda):=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}$ (equivalently in the level-one symmetric residue convention of the regime) and define the **degree** of a standard tableau inductively by $\deg(\varnothing):=0$ and, for $d>0$, $\deg(T):=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+d_A(\mu)$ where $A$ is the node of $T$ containing $d$.

The definition asserts, and proves below in [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]], that $\{v_T:T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)\}$ is a homogeneous $F$-basis of $S(\mu)$ making it a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module whose $q$-character is $\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_T q^{\deg T}i_T$; forgetting the grading recovers the ungraded cell module. **Convention.** This is the LEFT Murphy cell module, obtained from the right cellular datum by $h\cdot m=m h^*$. Forgetting its grading, [[thm-dj-bridge-murphy-cell-is-the-same-shape-specht-dual]] identifies it with the star-contragredient dual of the same-shape independently defined ordinary Dipper–James Specht module $P(\mu)$. Separately, [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]] gives $S(\mu)\cong P(\mu')^{\theta}$ after the same left-module conversion. These are two proved module comparisons, not the identification of an untwisted conjugate module. The sign pullback may change ordinary residue content from $-\alpha$ to $\alpha$; these ungraded comparisons do not assert homogeneity of the ordinary form or of a raw Hecke sign automorphism in the fixed transported grading. The labelling of simples by $e$-restricted or $e$-regular partitions is NOT asserted here; it is determined by the head-classification theorem later on this page.

No choice is used in the definition.
items.strategy: This is a definition with its construction; the asserted basis, homogeneity and module structure are discharged by [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]], and the ideal/cellular facts by [[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]]. The degree recursion is the source's (4.33); the vectors $v_T$ depend a priori on the chosen reduced decompositions, and the theorem proves the resulting grading is well defined. The same-shape ordinary duality is established by the perfect star-balanced cross-pairing of [[thm-dj-bridge-murphy-cell-is-the-same-shape-specht-dual]], which does not require a nondegenerate self-form. The separate conjugate comparison is the explicit universal signed isomorphism of [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]. Convert both right modules through star; because theta commutes with star, finite duality and sign pullback keep their stated positions. No unsupported historical source20 convention is used. No choice. Use the LEFT-handed Murphy basis: if the supplied cellular datum is right-handed, apply its anti-involution to every basis identity. Then H z_mu is a left cyclic cell module, z_T=T_w z_mu and v_T=psi_w z_mu are left actions, consistent with the left KLR modules and right-append corner functors used throughout. No identification of a right module with a left module without this conversion is made.

items.title: The integral form of the cyclotomic Hecke-KLR block
items.statement: Let $K$ be a characteristic-zero field in branch (C0) of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]] and fix, for each residue content $\alpha$, the Khovanov-Lauda generators $\{e(i)\}$, $\{y_r\}$, $\{\psi_r\}$ of the block $H^\Lambda_\alpha(K)$ of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]], i.e. the $\rho_\alpha$-images of the KLR generators ([[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]], [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]]), in a fixed admissible local normalising series. Define $$H^\Lambda_\alpha(\mathbb Z):=\bigl\langle e(i),\ y_r,\ \psi_r\ \bigr\rangle_{\mathbb Z}\subseteq H^\Lambda_\alpha(K)$$ to be the $\mathbb Z$-subring generated by them. It is the $\mathbb Z$-span of the same finite normal forms (in the Khovanov-Lauda generators) that span $H^\Lambda_\alpha(K)$ over $K$, hence a free $\mathbb Z$-module and a lattice; the generator degrees give it a grading, and the base-change maps $$K\otimes_{\mathbb Z}H^\Lambda_\alpha(\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_\alpha(K),\qquad F\otimes_{\mathbb Z}H^\Lambda_\alpha(\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H^\Lambda_\alpha(F)$$ sending $1\otimes e(i)\mapsto e(i)$, $1\otimes y_r\mapsto y_r$, $1\otimes\psi_r\mapsto\psi_r$ are isomorphisms of graded algebras for every field $F$ of sub-branch (CP) with a primitive $e$-th root of unity, the second being the reduction modulo $p$. The direct sums over $\alpha$ give the integral form of the tower. No choice is used.
items.strategy: Use the exact integer type-A KLR presentation with generator images in each characteristic-zero sector. Integer PBW straightening spans its image by ordered dot monomials times crossing words and word idempotents. Dot nilpotence in the finite characteristic-zero standard cyclotomic quotient bounds every position; finitely many words give finitely many nonzero spanning monomials. Their Z-span is closed under integer straightening and is torsion-free inside the characteristic-zero algebra. First descend to Q: the map from the Q KLR presentation to the generator image becomes the actual BK isomorphism after extending to K; faithful field extension makes it an isomorphism already over Q. Thus the integer image is a full finite lattice in this Q-algebra, of rank equal to dim_K H_alpha(K), and K tensor this lattice is H_alpha(K). For EVERY content alpha at fixed rank the reduced named generators satisfy the integer relations and generate F tensor the lattice, giving a SURJECTION H_alpha(F) -> F tensor H_alpha(Z) via the actual field BK presentation. Consequently dim_F H_alpha(F) >= dim_K H_alpha(K) for every alpha, including zero sectors. Sum over all finitely many rank-d contents: both total dimensions equal ell^d d! by the late field basis theorem. All individual nonnegative differences therefore vanish, proving every surjection is an isomorphism. Rankzero gives the singleton unit lattice; the levelzero positive-rank quotient is zero. Homogeneity of generators and relations supplies the integer grading. This is the complete applicable BK2008 Theorems6.1/6.4 proof route, without inferring an individual block dimension directly from total dimension alone. No choice.

items.title: Degree and codegree of standard tableaux
items.strategy: Separate below and above counts. Removing the removable i-node A changes the total addable-minus-removable count by the Cartan column, and A becomes an addable node in mu^A. Splitting all remaining i-nodes into strictly above and strictly below A gives d_A(mu)+d^A(mu^A)=d_i(mu)+1. Induction from the empty diagram and the same local boundary changes gives d_i(mu)=(Lambda0-alpha,alpha_i). Expanding defect(alpha)-defect(alpha-alpha_i) using (alpha_i,alpha_i)=2 gives d_i(mu)+1. Induct on the number of nodes in the degree/codegree recursion to obtain their sum equal to defect. For a horizontal terminal brick, codegree counts strictly ABOVE it: the first row has no such nodes; an e-brick contains every residue once and above boundary addable/removable contributions cancel. This proves both brick clauses. Check e2 shape(2): below degree1, above codegree0, defect1; shape(1,1): degree0, above codegree1, defect1. items.title: A graded algebra isomorphism transports the graded module category, its Grothendieck groups and its dualities
items.statement:
Let $\rho:R\to H$ be an isomorphism of finite-dimensional unital $\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebras. Restriction of scalars along $\rho$ is an equivalence of graded left module categories which is exact, sends finite-dimensional modules to finite-dimensional modules, sends a shift $M\{r\}$ to $M\{r\}$, sends finitely generated graded projectives to finitely generated graded projectives, preserves composition multiplicities of graded simples (with shifts), and identifies the graded Hom pairings $\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}$ of [[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]]. It therefore induces $A$-module isomorphisms $K_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to K_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ and $G_0^{\rm gr}(R)\to G_0^{\rm gr}(H)$ intertwining the Cartan homomorphisms and the forgetful maps $\zeta$.

If moreover $\rho$ intertwines fixed anti-automorphisms $\ast_R$ and $\ast_H$ (i.e. $\rho(x^{\ast_R})=\rho(x)^{\ast_H}$), then the transported functor intertwines the two diagram dualities $D_\psi$ and the two projective Hom-dualities $\#$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]], and hence preserves normalized self-dual simples and normalized self-dual indecomposable projectives.

**Application.** For each nonzero content sector choose the actual graded block isomorphism rho_alpha. DEFINE the Hecke duality by star_H=rho_alpha star_R rho_alpha^{-1}. This is a grading-preserving anti-involution, fixing the NAMED images of e(i),y_r,psi_r, and rho_alpha intertwines it by definition. Thus the preceding duality conclusion applies blockwise. This does not identify star_H with the raw cellular anti-involution that fixes affine Hecke generators, and does not infer that a product is fixed merely because its factors are fixed.
items.strategy: An algebra isomorphism gives inverse exact restriction-of-scalars functors, identity on the underlying graded vector spaces. It preserves shifts, finite dimension and finite free modules; retracts of finite free modules remain projective. Graded Hom spaces agree by the identity on maps, hence composition multiplicities, K0/G0, Cartan and forgetful maps agree. For finite duals, (a f)(m)=f(star_R(a)m) matches the transported formula because rho star_R=star_H rho; the identical substitution in Hom_R(P,R) identifies projective Hom duals. In the application define star_H by conjugation, which proves anti-multiplicativity and involutivity immediately; generator fixation is fixation of the rho-images. Products are reversed by star_H, so no claim about the raw affine-Hecke cellular star is used. This exact computation proves the transported self-dual and degree-zero head normalization clauses. No choice.

items.title: Shifted degrees and Garnir exchanges for standard tableaux
items.statement:
In the situation of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]:

1. If $T\xrightarrow{\,r\,}S$ (i.e. both tableaux are standard, $S=s_rT$, and $r$ occupies an earlier row-reading node than $r+1$, as in [[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]]), then $\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$, where $i_T=(i_1,\dots,i_d)$ and $a$ is the Cartan matrix of the regime.
2. More generally, if $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ is a reduced decomposition, then $\deg(T)-\deg(t^\mu)=\deg\bigl(\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}e(i_{t^\mu})\bigr)$ in the grading of [[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]].
3. If $T$ is the $(a,b)$-Garnir tableau with entry $r$ in the node $(a,b)$, and $S$ is a standard $\mu$-tableau with $S\lhd T$ and $i_S=i_{s_rT}$, then $\deg(S)-\deg(T)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ as well.

No choice is used.
items.strategy: 1 is [BKW, Proposition 3.13]: reduce to $r=d-1$ and compare the two expressions for $\deg(T)$ and $\deg(S)$; the difference is $d_B(\mu^A)-d_B(\mu)$ for the nodes $A$ (containing $d$) and $B$ (containing $d-1$), and the four residue cases (equal residues, adjacent single edge, the $e=2$ double edge, and non-adjacent) give exactly $-2,1,2,0=-a_{i_{d-1}i_d}$. 2 is [BKW, Corollary 3.14], obtained from 1 by multiplying the adjacent transpositions of the reduced word and adding the degrees $\deg(\psi_re(i_T))$. 3 is [BKW, Proposition 3.16]: using the tableau-order Lemma 3.9 reduce to a two-row Garnir belt; the exchange condition $i_S=i_{s_rT}$ splits the belt into bricks of size divisible by $e$ plus at most one exceptional brick per row; Lemma 3.15 computes $\operatorname{codeg}(S)$ and $\operatorname{codeg}(T)$ by the congruence classes of $b$ modulo $e$, and the difference is $-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ in each case. All steps are finite residue and brick computations; no choice. For the strict Garnir case retain the maximal standard belt tableau and strict Bruhat lower condition. Reduce to a two-row belt ending at its final node by the agreement-outside-belt lemma. Remove complete horizontal e-bricks using the ABOVE codegree lemma. The lower tableau has residual codegree -1 if b is nonzero modulo e and 0 otherwise. The Garnir tableau has codegree0/1 for e>2, and1/2 for e=2, respectively. Their difference gives degree1/2 in the single/double-edge cases. Equal-color degree in a standard exchange remains -2, from the Cartan diagonal; it is not assigned +2.

items.title: The graded Specht module has a homogeneous tableau basis
items.statement:
Keep the notation of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]]; the vectors $v_T=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ may a priori depend on the chosen reduced decompositions $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$. Then:

1. For every $\mu$-tableau $T$ one has $v_T=\sum_{S\unlhd T}a_Sz_S$ with $a_T\ne0$ when $T$ is standard; hence the standard vectors form a basis of $S(\mu)$ triangular with respect to the standard basis $\{z_T\}$ of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].
2. If $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}=s_{t_1}\cdots s_{t_m}$ are two reduced decompositions of the same $w_T$, then $\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}z_\mu-\psi_{t_1}\cdots\psi_{t_m}z_\mu=\sum_{S\unlhd T,\ i_S=i_T,\ \deg S=\deg T}a_Sv_S$; in particular the grading on $S(\mu)$ defined by $\deg(v_T):=\deg(T)$ is independent of the choices.
3. For every $r$ the vectors $e(i)v_T$, $y_rv_T$ and $\psi_rv_T$ are homogeneous, with $$e(i)v_T=\delta_{i,i_T}v_T,\qquad \deg(y_rv_T)=\deg(y_r)+\deg(T),\qquad \deg(\psi_rv_T)=\deg(\psi_re(i_T))+\deg(T).$$ Hence $S(\mu)$ is a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module with homogeneous basis $\{v_T\}$ and $q$-character $\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_{T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)}q^{\deg T}i_T$; forgetting the grading recovers the ungraded cell module of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]].

No choice beyond the finite selections of reduced decompositions is used; the resulting graded isomorphism class is independent of them by (2).
items.strategy: Follow [BKW, §4.2-4.3]: (1) expand $\psi_{r_1}\cdots\psi_{r_m}z_\mu$ in the standard basis using the quadratic relation, the dot-sliding relations and Lemma 4.1 ($y_rz_\mu=0$, $X_rz_\mu=\xi^{i_r}z_\mu$), and use Proposition 4.3 (triangularity of the $z$-basis) to identify the leading coefficient, which is nonzero exactly for standard $T$. (2) By Matsumoto's theorem it suffices to compare two words differing by one braid relation; the quadratic/braid relations express the difference as a combination of shorter words with the stated weight and degree, and induction on length plus (1) gives the claim. (3) Compute $y_rv_T$ and $\psi_rv_T$ by moving the generators through the reduced word using the mixed relations; every occurring vector has weight $i_T$ or $i_{s_rT}$ and the degrees follow from [[prop-shifted-degrees-and-garnir-exchanges-for-standard-tableaux]] (1) and the definition of $\deg(T)$; the codegree identities of [[lem-degree-and-codegree-of-standard-tableaux]] supply the bookkeeping in the terminal/Garnir cases. The $q$-character formula is then immediate from the homogeneous basis, and forgetting the grading gives the ungraded cell module by construction. This is [BKW, Theorem 4.10] restated; the independence statement is its part (i). No choice.

items.axiom_use: None: finite integer PBW, crossing straightening, finite rational kernels and the choice-free regular-trace/finite-root-field head helper.
items.statement:
Fix the level-one type-A integer KLR presentation, charge $0$, and finite quantum characteristic $e\in\{2,3,\ldots\}$. Let $K$ be any characteristic-zero field in the specified Hecke regime, let $\lambda$ be the specified partition, and let $S_K(\lambda)$ be the LEFT graded Murphy cell Specht module with its specified initial cyclic generator $z_K$. Then there is a finite-dimensional graded module $S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$ for the rational KLR algebra, with a specified homogeneous cyclic vector $z_{\mathbb Q}$, and a graded generator-preserving isomorphism $K\otimes_{\mathbb Q} S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)\cong S_K(\lambda)$. The rational module is explicitly presented by the initial weight, dot and horizontal crossing relations, together with one homogeneous rational relation for each Garnir belt. Each of these relations is the unique vector with Garnir coefficient $1$ in the kernel of a finite matrix with integer entries, obtained from crossing operators in the integer row permutation module. It therefore depends only on the integer presentation, not on a choice of $K$ or of a root of unity.

If the specified normalized simple head $D_K(\lambda)$ is nonzero and absolutely simple, this construction, combined with the local cyclic-head descent lemma, defines its initial-generator image line over $\mathbb Q$ up to scalar. The orbit of that image under the finite integer cyclotomic algebra is a lattice of rank $\dim_K D_K(\lambda)$.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]] gives the affine KLR PBW basis. Dot slides remove one crossing from correction terms, quadratic moves remove two, and three-term braid corrections remove three. Preferred reduced expressions differ by terms with strictly fewer crossings.

[F2] [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]] fixes the integer coefficients and the source BK/BKW crossing convention $\psi=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$. This proof uses that convention directly; it does not identify KMR's reversed-orientation crossing with it.

[F3] [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]] supplies the LEFT Murphy cell Specht module's homogeneous standard basis $v_T=\psi_{w_T}z_K$ and triangularity: for every tableau $T$, $v_T$ is a combination of standard $v_U$ with $w_U\le w_T$ in strong Bruhat order. Idempotents and grading restrict this expansion to the vector's weight and degree.

[F4] The specified initial vector has weight $i^\lambda$, all dots kill it, and a crossing kills it when its two successive entries occupy the same initial row. These are the initial-generator relations in the reviewed BKW construction, not conditions imposed on an arbitrary vector in a simple.

[F5] [[lem-integer-cyclic-presentation-descends-the-simple-head-generator-line]] proves characteristic-zero radical base change by the regular trace pairing, hence descends a rational cyclic module's normalized simple head and its specified generator image, and proves the lattice rank.

[F6] [[def-integral-form-of-the-cyclotomic-hecke-klr-block]] gives the finite free integer cyclotomic algebra used in step 5.2. The local PBW straightening used before that quotient is integral: its monic moves have integer coefficients, and independence follows by rational scalar extension of the supplied PBW basis.

## Proof

**Given:** The stated level-one integer presentation, the specified LEFT cell module and its initial generator, and F1–F5. No Axiom of Choice is used.

1.1 Put $\kappa=0$ in the residue formulas below. Work first in the affine content algebra $R_{\mathbb Z}$ before the cyclotomic quotient. For each row of $\lambda$, the successive residue segment has a one-dimensional integral module on which its word idempotent is $1$ and its dots and internal crossings are $0$. The KLR relations hold: successive colours are distinct, their quadratic at zero dots is $0$, and a possible three-strand repeated-endpoint pattern occurs only for $e=2$, where its double-edge braid correction also vanishes at zero dots. Induce the tensor product of these segment modules, and shift its generator $m_0$ to degree $\deg(T_0)$, where $T_0$ is row reading. Denote the result by $M_{\mathbb Z}$. [F2, construct, algebra]

1.2 Let $P$ be the Young row subgroup. Choose reduced expressions compatible with the unique decomposition $w=d p$, with $d$ a minimal representative for $S_d/P$ and $p\in P$, and $\ell(w)=\ell(d)+\ell(p)$. F1 then makes the inducing bimodule free over the row algebra on the minimal-representative words. Tensoring the one-dimensional row modules shows that $M_{\mathbb Z}$ has the integral basis $m_T=\psi_{w_T}m_0$ indexed by all row-strict tableaux $T$. Its cyclic presentation is exactly the initial weight, dot and horizontal-crossing relations. In particular all generator-action matrices on this finite basis have integer entries. Put $M_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q\otimes M_{\mathbb Z}$; scalar extension gives $M_K=K\otimes M_{\mathbb Q}$. By F4, there is a surjective graded map $\pi_K:M_K\to S_K(\lambda)$ carrying $m_0$ exactly to $z_K$. [F1, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

1.3 Crossing straightening gives a filtration useful below: a word with at most $N$ crossings applied to $m_0$ is a combination of $m_U$ with $\ell(w_U)\le N$. Move dots right, reduce nonreduced words by quadratic and Coxeter moves, compare reduced words, and split off the right row subgroup as in step 1.2. Positive dot powers kill $m_0$; a nontrivial row factor ends in an internal crossing and also kills $m_0$. Every correction has fewer crossings. In particular if $s_rT$ is row-strict and $\ell(w_{s_rT})=\ell(w_T)+1$, then $\psi_r m_T=m_{s_rT}$ plus terms of strictly smaller crossing length, with leading coefficient exactly $1$. If $s_rT$ is not row-strict, its possible leading term is killed by the right row factor and only shorter terms remain. [F1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.1 Fix a Garnir node $A=(a,b)$ with $(a+1,b)\in\lambda$. Its belt consists of the row-$a$ suffix $X$ beginning at column $b$ and row-$(a+1)$ prefix $Y$ ending at column $b$. The entries in these nodes in $T_0$ form one consecutive interval $J=\{u,\ldots,v\}$: the suffix ends at the last position of row $a$, immediately followed by the prefix at the beginning of row $a+1$. Let $G_A$ agree with $T_0$ outside the belt and fill $Y$ first, then $X$, increasingly with $J$. It is row-strict and nonstandard. This $G_A$ is the nonstandard belt filling used for the rational-kernel presentation; it is distinct from the maximal STANDARD Garnir tableau in [[def-tableau-domination-order-garnir-tableaux-and-bricks]]. [construct, algebra]

2.2 Among ALL row-strict tableaux agreeing with $T_0$ outside this belt, $G_A$ is the only nonstandard one. For columns $c<b$, the upper entry is an unchanged number less than $u$, hence less than every changed lower entry. For columns $c>b$, the lower entry, if present, is unchanged and greater than $v$, hence greater than every changed upper entry. Comparisons with the row above or the row below have the same strict bounds, and every other column comparison is unchanged. Thus only column $b$ can fail. It fails precisely when the first upper-belt entry exceeds the last lower-belt entry. Since each of the two rows is increasing, this is equivalent to every upper-belt entry exceeding every lower-belt entry, and hence to the unique filling $G_A$. [step 2.1, algebra]

2.3 On $J$, the residue word $i(G_A)$ is one successive-residue segment. Along $Y$ the residues increase by $1$; its final node $(a+1,b)$ has residue $\kappa+b-a-1$. The first node of $X$, $(a,b)$, has residue $\kappa+b-a$, and the rest again increase by $1$. Consequently $i(G_A)_r\ne i(G_A)_{r+1}$ for every $u\le r<v$, including $e=2$. This distinctness, rather than any braid normalization, is essential. [F2, step 2.1, algebra]

2.4 Let $\delta_A=\deg(\psi_{w_{G_A}}e(i^\lambda))+\deg(T_0)$ and let $T_A^{\mathbb Q}$ be the span of those integral basis vectors $m_T$ for which $T$ agrees with $T_0$ outside the belt, has weight $i(G_A)$, and has homogeneous degree $\delta_A$. It includes $m_{G_A}$. The use of the entire weight-degree slice avoids any brick-classification assumption. Write $T_A^K=K\otimes T_A^{\mathbb Q}$. [F1, step 1.2, step 2.1, construct]

2.5 The vector $\pi_K(m_{G_A})$ is a combination of images of standard basis vectors in $T_A^K$. Indeed F3 gives standard $U$ with $w_U\le w_{G_A}$. The permutation $w_{G_A}$ belongs to the parabolic subgroup generated by $s_u,\ldots,s_{v-1}$, since it permutes only $J$. Every Bruhat-smaller permutation belongs to this same subgroup: choose a reduced word for $w_{G_A}$ in these generators, and use the defining subword characterization of strong Bruhat order. Hence $U$ agrees with $T_0$ outside the belt. Weight idempotents discard different words, and homogeneity discards different degrees, leaving exactly the standard vectors in the slice of step 2.4. By step 2.2, every other vector of the slice is standard; by F3 its image is part of the standard Specht basis and is linearly independent. Therefore $\ker(\pi_K|_{T_A^K})$ is precisely one-dimensional, including the case where the image of $m_{G_A}$ is zero. [F3, step 2.2, step 2.4, algebra]

3.1 For every $u\le r<v$, the image $\psi_r T_A^K$ in $M_K$ is spanned by standard row-strict belt tableaux. To see the support assertion, choose reduced words for all belt permutations using only $s_u,\ldots,s_{v-1}$. Straightening a crossing supported in this interval never introduces a crossing outside it; factoring a right row permutation also uses only this interval. Thus every resulting row-strict basis tableau agrees outside the belt. The image has fixed weight $s_r i(G_A)$, which differs from $i(G_A)$ by step 2.3. Its support cannot include the sole nonstandard belt tableau $G_A$. Hence the entire image has standard support by step 2.2, and $\pi_K$ is injective on its span by F3. [F1, F3, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 2.4, algebra]

3.2 If $x\in\ker(\pi_K|_{T_A^K})$, then $\pi_K(\psi_r x)=\psi_r\pi_K(x)=0$. The injectivity in step 3.1 implies $\psi_r x=0$ in $M_K$ for every inside-belt crossing. Thus this one-dimensional Specht-kernel line lies in $B_A^K:=\bigcap_{r=u}^{v-1}\ker(\psi_r:T_A^K\to M_K)$. [step 2.5, step 3.1, algebra]

3.3 The $m_{G_A}$ coefficient map is injective on $B_A^K$. Suppose a nonzero $x\in B_A^K$ has that coefficient zero. Choose a tableau $T$ with nonzero coefficient in $x$ whose crossing length $N=\ell(w_T)$ is maximal. It is standard by step 2.2. Record membership in $X$ or $Y$ for the successive numbers $u,\ldots,v$ as a binary word. Unless this word is all $Y$ then all $X$, it has an adjacent occurrence $XY$; that excluded word is exactly $G_A$. Choose such an occurrence at $r,r+1$. Swapping them preserves row strictness because they lie in different rows and are consecutive numbers; it increases permutation length by $1$, because $r$ is in the earlier row. Its weight becomes $s_r i(G_A)\ne i(G_A)$, so it cannot be $G_A$ and is also standard by step 2.2. By step 1.3, the coefficient of $m_{s_rT}$ in $\psi_r x$ at length $N+1$ is precisely the nonzero coefficient of $m_T$ in $x$. A lower-length input cannot reach length $N+1$; a different equal-length input has a different possible leading tableau because $s_r$ is injective; and its correction terms have smaller length. Therefore $\psi_r x\ne0$, contradicting $x\in B_A^K$. [step 1.3, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 3.2, algebra]

3.4 Consequently $\dim_K B_A^K\le1$, while step 3.2 gives a nonzero line inside it. Thus $B_A^K=\ker(\pi_K|_{T_A^K})$. Define $B_A^{\mathbb Q}$ using the same intersection of crossing kernels over $\mathbb Q$. These are kernels of a single finite stacked matrix with integer entries on the explicitly selected integral row-strict bases. Row reduction over $\mathbb Q$ commutes with extension to $K$, so $B_A^K=K\otimes B_A^{\mathbb Q}$. It follows that $B_A^{\mathbb Q}$ is one-dimensional and has a unique rational vector $h_A$ with coefficient $1$ on $m_{G_A}$. Its scalar extension is exactly the Specht-kernel vector with that normalization. This is an explicit rational linear-system construction of the relation, not an assumption that a chosen vector belongs to a rational form. [step 1.2, step 3.2, step 3.3, algebra]

4.1 Every other row-strict belt tableau has strictly smaller crossing length than $G_A$. Outside the belt there are no inversions involving belt entries because the belt interval is consecutive in row reading and its values form $J$. Inside, inversions are exactly upper/lower pairs with the upper entry larger. The tableau $G_A$ has all $|X||Y|$ such inversions, whereas every other filling loses at least one. Hence $h_A=m_{G_A}+\sum_{U:\,\ell(w_U)<\ell(w_{G_A})}c_U m_U$ with rational $c_U$, and it is homogeneous of degree $\delta_A$ by its definition in the slice. [step 2.1, step 2.4, step 3.4, algebra]

4.2 Put $S_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{univ}}=M_{\mathbb Q}/\sum_A R_{\mathbb Q}h_A$. We prove standard spanning locally. For any nonstandard row-strict $T$, choose a vertical inversion at $(a,b),(a+1,b)$. All entries in its upper suffix $X$ exceed all entries in its lower prefix $Y$. Its Garnir factor $G_A$ therefore satisfies $T=wG_A$ with $w=w_Tw_{G_A}^{-1}$ and $\ell(w)=\ell(w_T)-\ell(w_{G_A})$: reordering the contiguous belt's one-line list from $X,Y$ to $Y,X$ removes precisely its $|X||Y|$ cross inversions, while preserving within-part and outside comparisons. Reduced-word straightening and the relation $h_A=0$ replace $m_T$ by words with fewer than $\ell(w_T)$ crossings, by step 4.1. The filtration of step 1.3 expresses these as row-strict vectors of strictly smaller length. Induction proves that standard vectors span the quotient. [F1, step 1.3, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

4.3 Scalar extension of the rational quotient presentation gives $S_K^{\mathrm{univ}}=K\otimes S_{\mathbb Q}^{\mathrm{univ}}$. Every $h_A$ lies in $\ker\pi_K$ by step 3.4, so $\pi_K$ induces a surjection $S_K^{\mathrm{univ}}\to S_K(\lambda)$ preserving the generator and grading. The source is spanned by the standard vectors by step 4.2, and their images are the linearly independent standard Specht basis by F3. Hence this map is an isomorphism. In particular the rational module is finite-dimensional, has its standard basis, and its generator maps exactly to $z_K$. [F3, step 3.4, step 4.2, algebra]

5.1 The rational module factors through the cyclotomic quotient. Each specified cyclotomic relation acts as zero after extension to $K$, because the module in step 4.3 is the specified cyclotomic Hecke cell Specht module. The matrix of that action on the rational standard basis has rational entries; faithful field extension forces it to be zero already over $\mathbb Q$. Denote this rational cyclotomic module by $S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$, with generator $z_{\mathbb Q}$ the class of $m_0$. This identifies the required rational initial cyclic generator, not merely the unpointed module's isomorphism class. [step 4.3, algebra]

5.2 If an integer cyclic quotient is desired for F5, take the saturated generator annihilator $I_{\mathbb Z}=\{a\in A_{\mathbb Z}:a z_{\mathbb Q}=0\}$ in the finite integer cyclotomic algebra of [[def-integral-form-of-the-cyclotomic-hecke-klr-block]]. It is a homogeneous left ideal, and $A_{\mathbb Z}/I_{\mathbb Z}$ identifies with the integral orbit $A_{\mathbb Z}z_{\mathbb Q}\subset S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$. Its rational span is the entire rational module by cyclicity, so $\mathbb Q\otimes(A_{\mathbb Z}/I_{\mathbb Z})\cong S_{\mathbb Q}(\lambda)$ with the specified generator. Clearing denominators in each $h_A$ is also possible, but no unsaturated integer quotient or integral Specht-freeness theorem is needed. [step 5.1, algebra]

5.3 Apply F5 to this pointed rational form and the supplied absolutely simple normalized head. Its radical-basechange proof gives a rational normalized head with the image of $z_{\mathbb Q}$; absolute Schur makes every quotient map to the fixed head differ only by a scalar. Its integral-algebra orbit is finitely generated and torsion-free, with rational span that head, so its rank is exactly the head's $K$-dimension. This establishes the precise requested initial-generator line and lattice statement over arbitrary characteristic-zero $K$. No three-brick identity, unproved R-matrix formula, arbitrary-vector rational form, or change of the specified generator enters the argument. [F5, step 5.1, step 5.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Graded Specht restriction has the removable-node filtration
items.statement:
Keep the notation of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]], let $\mu$ be a partition of $d$, $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$, and let $i\in I=\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$. Let $A_1,\dots,A_c$ be the removable $i$-nodes of $\mu$ ordered from bottom to top, and let $\mu^{A_m}=\mu\setminus A_m$. Write $E_i:=E_i^{\rm basic}$ for the restriction functor $N\mapsto e(\alpha-\alpha_i,\alpha_i)N$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]] (equivalently the $i$-part of the tower restriction of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]). Then $E_iS(\mu)$ has a filtration $$0=V_0\subset V_1\subset\cdots\subset V_c=E_iS(\mu)$$ of graded $R^\Lambda_{\alpha-\alpha_i}$-modules with $V_m/V_{m-1}\cong S(\mu^{A_m})\{d_{A_m}(\mu)\}$ for $1\le m\le c$.

Equivalently, the restriction of $S(\mu)$ to the previous rank has the removable-node filtration of [BKW, Theorem 4.11] over ALL removable nodes, and $E_i$ selects the removable-$i$-node part. No choice is used.
items.strategy: By [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]] the module $S(\mu)$ has the homogeneous tableau basis $\{v_T\}$ with $v_T\in e(i_T)S(\mu)$, so the idempotent projection $e(\alpha-\alpha_i,\alpha_i)S(\mu)$ is spanned by those $v_T$ whose last letter is $i$, i.e. whose maximal entry $d$ occupies a removable $i$-node. Set $V_m:=\operatorname{span}\{v_T:\ d\text{ lies in }A_1\cup\cdots\cup A_m\}$; each $V_m$ is a graded $R^\Lambda_{\alpha-\alpha_i}$-submodule because the generators $y_r,\psi_r$ of the previous rank act by the degree-preserving formulas of [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]] (3). The ungraded quotient identification $V_m/V_{m-1}\cong S(\mu^{A_m})$ is [AM, Proposition 1.9] as recalled in [BKW, Theorem 4.11]: deleting the maximal entry from a standard tableau with $d$ in $A_m$ gives a standard $\mu^{A_m}$-tableau, and the map $v_T+V_{m-1}\mapsto v_{T_{\le d-1}}$ is an isomorphism of $H^\Lambda_{d-1}$-modules; the grading shift is computed from the degree recursion $\deg(T)=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+d_{A_m}(\mu)$, which is exactly the shift $d_{A_m}(\mu)$. The passage from the whole restriction to $E_i$ is the idempotent decomposition $\operatorname{Res}=\bigoplus_iE_i$ of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]] and the definition of $E_i$; order the $i$-nodes bottom to top as in the source. This is [BKW, Theorem 4.11] and [BK 2009, Proposition 5.5]; the independent treatment of the (dual) induced filtration is [Hu-Mathas, Main Theorem]. No choice.

items.title: Graded Specht classes realize the standard Fock vectors
items.statement: In the regime of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], let $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}:G_0^{\rm gr}(H^{\Lambda})\to V_A(\Lambda_0)^\vee$ be the transported identification of [[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]], and let $S_\mu:=\pi(M_\mu)$ be the standard monomial image of the standard Fock vector $M_\mu$ of [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]] under the projection to the basic module. Then for every partition $\mu$ with content $\alpha$, $$\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}\bigl([S(\mu)]\bigr)=S_\mu .$$ In other words, the class of the graded Specht module of [[def-graded-specht-module-by-homogeneous-standard-tableaux]] is the standard Fock vector in the fixed level-one convention. This holds in both branches (C0) and (CP). No choice beyond the inherited suppliers is used.
items.strategy: Use the canonical native11 normalization throughout, not the KK map. At content beta let h_i(beta)=<h_i,Lambda0-beta>. The actual removable-node filtration computes BASIC restriction as sum_A q^{d_A(mu)}[S(mu minus A)]. Canonical E_i is q^{-1-h_i(beta)} times that restriction. For a removable i-node A the omitted removable A gives d_A(mu)+d^A(mu)=h_i(beta)+1, where d^A counts addable-minus-removable i-nodes strictly ABOVE A. Thus E_can[S(mu)]=sum_A q^{-d^A(mu)}[S(mu minus A)]. The symmetric linear-J Fock model and its field orthogonal projection supplied by the declared quantum9/23 interfaces satisfy precisely E_i pi(M_mu)=sum_A q^{-d^A(mu)}pi(M_(mu minus A)). Induct from the vacuum. The canonical transported map intertwines E_can, so all E_i kill the difference at positive root degree. Inside the irreducible Q(q) highest-weight module a nonzero vector killed by every E_i generates a highest-weight submodule; at a lower weight it cannot contain the original highest vector, contradicting irreducibility. Therefore the difference vanishes. Torsion-freeness of the restricted integral dual makes this equality valid over A. The argument uses only the declared current symmetric-model canonical recursion, never the source's bare-restriction recursion under a different normalization. It works in both field branches; q is independent of the Hecke parameter. No new choice.

items.title: The restricted graded Specht classes form a basis of the module Grothendieck group
items.statement: In the stated nondegenerate level-one regime and each residue content alpha, the classes [S(lambda)] indexed by RESTRICTED shapes lambda form an A-basis of G0^gr(H_alpha). Under Psi_can they correspond to the restricted standard coordinate functionals Std_lambda=pi(M_lambda), which form an A-basis of the UPPER integral dual lattice. Separately, all raw standard M_mu of that content form an A-basis of the ambient Fock standard lattice; their full projected family is generally redundant. No claim that Std_lambda is a basis of the lower lattice or that the field Gram denominator is an A-unit is made. Choice only as inherited.
items.strategy: The corrected canonical Specht theorem sends each restricted Specht class to Std_lambda. The earlier coordinate-functional lemma proves that restricted Std_lambda are an A-basis of the UPPER dual, by the dominance-unitriangular restricted D minor; the actual canonical native11 G0 identification is an isomorphism to exactly that restricted dual. Pull back this basis. The ambient raw M_mu basis is the original Fock definition and is not identified with its projected image. All content weight spaces are finite. No lower-lattice self-duality or assumed Gram determinant unit is used.

items.title: Graded decomposition numbers equal canonical-basis coefficients in characteristic zero
items.statement: In branch (C0) of the regime of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]], for every partition $\mu$ with content $\alpha$ and every $\lambda\in RP_\alpha$, the graded composition multiplicity satisfies $$[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q=d_{\lambda,\mu}(q),$$ where $d_{\lambda,\mu}$ is the level-one global-basis transition polynomial of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]; equivalently $[S(\mu)]=\sum_{\lambda\in RP_\alpha}d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$ in $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$, and $d_{\lambda,\mu}=0$ unless $\lambda\unlhd\mu$. Specializing $q=1$ gives Ariki's ungraded decomposition-number theorem $[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]=d_{\lambda,\mu}(1)$. Choice is inherited only through the QG-8 global-basis suppliers.
items.strategy: Apply the transported isomorphism $\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke}$ to the class of $S(\mu)$: by [[thm-graded-specht-classes-realize-standard-fock-vectors]] it equals $S_\mu$, and by [[lem-standard-fock-vectors-expand-in-the-upper-global-basis]] $S_\mu=\sum_{\lambda}d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)G^*(\lambda)$ with the same coefficients as the lower expansion. By [[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]] (2) the vectors $G^*(\lambda)$ are the images of the simple classes $[D(\lambda)]$, so applying $(\Psi_{\rm can}^{\rm Hecke})^{-1}$ yields $[S(\mu)]=\sum_\lambda d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)[D(\lambda)]$; the composition multiplicities are read off because the simple classes form a basis of the free $A$-module $G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_\alpha)$ ([[prop-qg8-categorification-transports-across-the-hecke-klr-bridge]] (2)). The dominance vanishing is the support statement of [[def-level-one-global-basis-transition-polynomials-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]]. The $q=1$ specialization is the forgetful map of [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]], and the ungraded statement is [BK 2009, Theorem 5.9] (Ariki). This is [BK 2009, Theorem 5.14 and Corollary 5.15], with [Kleshchev, Theorem 9.9] as the independent treatment. No new choice.

items.title: Reduction of characteristic-zero simple modules modulo p
items.strategy: Apply [[lem-rational-garnir-annihilator-lines-present-the-specified-specht-generator]] to the specified LEFT Murphy cell module and its initial homogeneous cyclic generator. Its finite integral row-permutation crossing matrices define a rational simultaneous Garnir-annihilator line; the strict crossing filtration proves standard spanning, and the actual homogeneous standard basis proves generator-preserving scalar-extension equality. It factors through the finite integer cyclotomic algebra by faithful rational scalar extension. Then [[lem-integer-cyclic-presentation-descends-the-simple-head-generator-line]] identifies the radical by the regular trace pairing, proves rational radical base change, and descends the specified simple head and initial-generator image. Absolute Schur makes every quotient map to the fixed normalized head differ only by a scalar. Thus the special vector lies in a scalar multiple of this proved rational form. No arbitrary-vector rational descent, KMR brick identity, or ordinary DJ comparison is used in this lattice step. The integer algebra orbit is finitely generated and torsion-free by the integral algebra theorem, spans the rational head by cyclicity, and is homogeneous; hence it is a full lattice of rank equal to the K-dimension. Word idempotents give graded direct summands, whose ranks survive tensoring with F, proving equality of graded word characters. Any other full homogeneous stable lattice has those same word-component ranks; the actual extremal-word character lemma proves G0 injectivity, so its reduction has the same G0 class. No assertion that all arbitrary K-lattices are literally commensurable without a rational/scalar identification is needed. Finally the restricted Specht classes are an A-basis of the UPPER dual lattice, have field-independent characters, and map under the corrected canonical identification to the same pi(M_mu). Character injectivity therefore shows that modules of equal characters over the two fields have equal images under Psi_can. Apply this to J(lambda) and the normalized characteristic-zero simple and invoke the characteristic-zero upper-basis theorem, proving part(3). No new choice beyond the declared sources.

items.title: Positive-characteristic Specht head and cyclotomic crystal labels agree
items.statement: In the positive-characteristic nondegenerate level-one regime, the normalized cellular head dotD(lambda) for each restricted partition lambda is isomorphic, with shift zero, to the normalized simple of the same right crystal label lambda. The reduction J(lambda) of the characteristic-zero normalized simple contains that crystal-labelled simple once, and has no constituents with cellular labels not dominated by lambda. Its G0 class is invariant under finite-module diagram duality. This proves the CP label comparison needed for the crystal-labelled adjustment matrix; it is not a positive-characteristic global-basis identification.
items.strategy:
Now let J(lambda) be the reduction of the characteristic-zero normalized simple of crystal label lambda, constructed using a rational Specht-generator lattice. Its graded word character equals that of the characteristic-zero simple. Choose an extremal word of this common character. In characteristic zero the reconstruction label is lambda; in positive characteristic the same word gives the same canonical B(Lambda) label. The displayed quotient is1 for the characteristic-zero simple, hence [J(lambda):D_crystal(lambda)]_q=1 in positive characteristic.

Independently, the corrected canonical Fock comparison and the upper expansion identify [J(lambda)] with the inverse image of the characteristic-zero upper vector. The restricted upper-transition minor is dominance-unitriangular. Invert it over Z[q,q^{-1}] and use the ACTUAL positive-characteristic cellular-head triangular expansion of restricted Specht classes. This gives [J(lambda)]=[D_cell(lambda)]+sum_{nu<lambda}a_nu(q)[D_cell(nu)]. These coefficients are the actual composition multiplicities because J(lambda) is a module; there is no asserted positivity from matrix inversion alone. Induct over a finite dominance refinement in the fixed root degree. Assume D_cell(nu)=D_crystal(nu) for the smaller labels. Since different crystal labels give different simple orbits, D_crystal(lambda) cannot be any smaller D_cell(nu). Its occurrence in J(lambda) therefore forces D_cell(lambda)=D_crystal(lambda). The coefficient1 forces shift0 as both chosen representatives are self-dual. This proves the CP label comparison before defining adjustment polynomials in the crystal-labelled basis.

The characteristic-zero simple D(lambda) is normalized for finite vector duality, so each word component e(nu)D(lambda) has a symmetric graded dimension: its Laurent polynomial is unchanged by v -> v^{-1}. The constructed J(lambda) has exactly the same graded word character. The descended generator-fixing anti-involution fixes every word idempotent; hence e(nu)D_psi J(lambda) is the graded vector dual of e(nu)J(lambda), and its graded dimension is the same symmetric polynomial. Therefore D_psi J(lambda) and J(lambda) have identical word characters. The completed local extremal-word character detection proves G0 character injectivity over the actual positive-characteristic field, so [D_psi J(lambda)]=[J(lambda)]. This proves bar invariance of its CLASS; no self-dual stable integral lattice is asserted.

items.title: Canonical bases do not solve arbitrary positive-characteristic decomposition numbers
items.statement: The characteristic-zero theorems of this page ([[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]], [[thm-graded-decomposition-numbers-equal-canonical-basis-coefficients-in-characteristic-zero]]) compute graded decomposition numbers of graded Specht modules as global-basis coefficients. In characteristic $p>0$ the factorization [[thm-positive-characteristic-decomposition-polynomials-factor-through-adjustment]] reduces the graded decomposition matrix to a product of the adjustment matrix and the SAME global-basis coefficients, but the adjustment matrix is generally nontrivial: the theorem computes no adjustment entry and asserts no identity adjustment matrix in general. Consequently the characteristic-zero canonical-basis theory does not by itself solve the decomposition-number problem in arbitrary positive characteristic; the general problem retains the boundary recorded in [[rem-general-modular-decomposition-numbers-are-not-determined-by-triangularity]] and [[rem-general-type-a-decomposition-numbers-remain-unsolved]]. This remark records the boundary; it carries no proof obligation and no choice principle.
items.strategy: Compare exactly what the two cited results determine: the characteristic-zero identifications compute $[S(\mu):D(\lambda)]_q$ as $d_{\lambda,\mu}(q)$, while the positive-characteristic factorization leaves the adjustment coefficients $a_{\lambda,\nu}(q)$ undetermined beyond bar-invariance, nonnegativity, unitriangularity and the dominance support of [[def-graded-adjustment-polynomials-in-positive-characteristic]]. The source's announced specialization to James's matrix concerns the degenerate parameter and is outside this page's regime (recorded in the coverage). No claim of a general positive-characteristic formula is made. Provenance: statement literature-derived; the remark is not consumed to prove any replacement.
